Scope of learning: this encounter · this object · broader experience
How can robots adapt to unfamiliar physical conditions?
Build and refine physical understanding through interaction.

across variations of the same task.
Research focus: learning from interaction, including failures and unexpected responses.
Train across physical conditions so the policy can use
environmental estimates to adapt its actions.
Enabling assumption: the policy can perform the required behavior under the tested conditions.
Completed baseline: predict mass from an initial RGB image.
Cubes vary in size; material and density are fixed.
Scope: one material, fixed density and friction, fixed camera. This tests interpolation over size.
One initial image supplies mass to the policy; execution uses state and force feedback.
Current implementation: the estimate and model weights stay fixed throughout execution.
How we make the estimator to train as it goes.

Proposed: use execution outcomes to improve task-relevant physical estimates.
of properties such as mass and friction.
Open question: what evidence should trigger an update, and what should change?
First test: does estimate refinement help?
Proposed simulation study: one object family, varied mass, fixed policy.
Keep shape, appearance and friction fixed.
Check policy performance with true mass.
Measure estimation error and task success under matched interaction budgets.
Later: CREST, broader materials and movement conditions, and learning across experience.

Proposed first controlled test: one cube geometry and appearance, fixed friction/pose and a frozen policy. Vary actual mass and initial estimation error. Before training an updater, check that the policy is capable under the chosen masses and that accurate supplied mass usefully changes performance. Check that permitted action/observation histories distinguish mass; finger normal compression is not vertical load, and failure alone does not identify mass. Compare fixed initial estimate, interaction-updated estimate and true-mass reference under matched probing and task budgets. True mass is an information reference, not a guaranteed performance ceiling. Keep evaluation mass out of deployment features. See presentations/interaction_adaptation_experiment.md for the proposed study. Related reading retained from the original draft: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09180 (lifelong multi-task RL, background reading rather than the estimator-update method).
